description: Analysis of peak suction events for high-rise building cladding design is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "experimental", published or maintained by Catherine Gorle, Stanford University (stanford.edu). This project has investigated the peak suction events that are relevant to high-rise building cladding design. High-resolution experiments were performed in the Wall of Wind NHERI EF under different atmospheric boundary layer conditions. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "experimental" project. Keywords: Wind hazards, wind loading, high-rise building, cladding design, wind tunnel test. Published 2021-03-05. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
